BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF KEPAHIANG,

Considering : a. that every citizen has the right to survival, to grow, and to develop, to obtain protection of personal self, honor and dignity as a complete human being in family life, society, nation and state; b. that every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence and discrimination; c. that all forms of acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their self-respect and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and natural disposition without discrimination; d. that violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency continues to increase both in quantity and quality, so that prevention, protection, recovery and law enforcement efforts are required; e. that legislation regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence requires the support of regulations and institutional apparatus at the Kepahiang Regency level that can guarantee its implementation; f. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, letter c, letter d and letter e, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Kepahiang concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence; In View of : 1. Article 18 Paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women) (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 3. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

Article 13
Other violence as referred to in Article 7 letter (f) is caused by:
a. threat of violence includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered or forced to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

Article 35
(1) In the event of a caught red-handed situation as referred to in Article 33 letter d, the community may secure the perpetrator before handing them over to the authorities.
(2) The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 28 letter b and letter e are, legally, to have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members;
(3) The role of the community as referred to in Article 34 paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.

CHAPTER V
P2TP2A
Article 38
(1) The Regional Government in order to provide services and protection to women and children victims of violence establishes P2TP2A.
(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing integrated protection to women and children from acts of violence.

CHAPTER VII
SAFE HOUSE
Article 46
(1) A safe house must be provided by the Social Affairs Office to handle cases of violence against women and children that pose a high risk to the safety of the victim.
(2) The management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall refer to the applicable laws and regulations.
(3) The financing for the management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be borne by the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD).

CHAPTER XI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 50
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. establishing family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level; b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights; d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE
First Part
Prevention

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Article 4
The scope of protection for women and children includes prevention efforts, services, recovery and empowerment.

Article 12
Exploitation as referred to in Article 7 letter (e) is carried out by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse

REGENT OF KEPAHIANG
DECIDES:
To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER X
FUNDING
Article 49
(1) Funding for protection activities for victims carried out by the Regional Government shall be charged to the APBD and/or other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Every SKPD related to programs and activities for the protection of women and children against acts of violence must allocate its budget.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER XI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 50
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. establishing family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level; b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights; d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

Article 43
The field of repatriation and reintegration into society as referred to in Article 39 paragraph (2) letter d has the following duties:
a. to coordinate with relevant agencies for the repatriation of victims;
b. to prepare progress reports on the process of accompanying repatriation and social recovery; and
c. to conduct monitoring for at least three months after the victim is returned to their family.

CHAPTER XI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 50
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. establishing family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level; b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights; d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Article 44
The field of legal aid services as referred to in Article 39 paragraph (2) letter e has the following duties:
a. to accompany and defend in every legal service process; and
b. to prepare reports on the progress of the handling of legal matters.

Article 21
Letter a Sufficiently clear.
Letter b What is meant by "right to basic services" includes, among others: the right to education, health and access to parents during the handling process.
Letter c What is meant by "right to equal protection" is related to status, citizenship, race, skin color, gender, language, belief, religion, politics, ethnicity or social life, property, disability, birth or other status.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e What is meant by "right to obtain freedom" is the freedom to express one's views on all matters, including those related to legal processes, care and temporary protection as well as identification and implementation of subsequent solutions.

Article 23
(1) Repatriation and reintegration services into society as referred to in Article 17 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
(2) Repatriation and reintegration services into society as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with relevant government and non-government agencies and institutions.

CHAPTER VIII
INFORMATION/REPORTING SYSTEM
Article 47
(1) SKPD whose main duties and functions are in the field of women's empowerment, family, family planning, and child protection shall implement an information/reporting system for the protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, which is reported to the Regent.
(2) The information/reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER X
FUNDING
Article 49
(1) Funding for protection activities for victims carried out by the Regional Government shall be charged to the APBD and/or other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Every SKPD related to programs and activities for the protection of women and children against acts of violence must allocate its budget.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Letter e Sufficiently clear.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, costs of returning home, health insurance, and education or skills training.
Letter g What is meant by "the right to social recovery" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER VII
SAFE HOUSE
Article 46
(1) A safe house must be provided by the Social Affairs Office to handle cases of violence against women and children that pose a high risk to the safety of the victim.
(2) The management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall refer to the applicable laws and regulations.
(3) The financing for the management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be borne by the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD).

CHAPTER V
P2TP2A
Article 38
(1) The Regional Government in order to provide services and protection to women and children victims of violence establishes P2TP2A.
(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing integrated protection to women and children from acts of violence.

Article 35
(1) In the event of a caught red-handed situation as referred to in Article 33 letter d, the community may secure the perpetrator before handing them over to the authorities.
(2) The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 28 letter b and letter e are, legally, to have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members;
(3) The role of the community as referred to in Article 34 paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.

Article 45
Further provisions regarding the development, mechanism, and networked working relationship of P2TP2A with related parties in handling violence against women and children shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing integrated protection to women and children from acts of violence.

CHAPTER XI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 50
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. establishing family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level; b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights; d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

Article 42
The field of social recovery services as referred to in Article 39 paragraph (2) letter c has the following duties:
a. providing assistance during the case handling process;
b. conducting counseling; and
c. facilitating the obtaining of a psychological certificate for the victim.

CHAPTER VII
SAFE HOUSE
Article 46
(1) A safe house must be provided by the Social Affairs Office to handle cases of violence against women and children that pose a high risk to the safety of the victim.
(2) The management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall refer to the applicable laws and regulations.
(3) The financing for the management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be borne by the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD).

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Article 45

Letter e Sufficiently clear.

b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.

4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.

16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

Article 4
The scope of protection for women and children includes prevention efforts, services, recovery and empowerment.

Article 13
Other violence as referred to in Article 7 letter (f) is caused by:
a. threat of violence includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered or forced to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

Article 20
Letter a What is meant by "the right to have one's dignity respected as a human being" is upholding human rights. Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain explanations, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, costs of returning home, health insurance, and education or skills training.
Letter g What is meant by "the right to social recovery" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.
Letter h What is meant by "the right to complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear.
Letter j What is meant by "the right to assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER XI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 50
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. establishing family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level; b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights; d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

Article 23
(1) Repatriation and reintegration services into society as referred to in Article 17 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
(2) Repatriation and reintegration services into society as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with relevant government and non-government agencies and institutions.

Article 35
(1) In the event of a caught red-handed situation as referred to in Article 33 letter d, the community may secure the perpetrator before handing them over to the authorities.
(2) The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 28 letter b and letter e are, legally, to have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members;
(3) The role of the community as referred to in Article 34 paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the return and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women and children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and defense for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights. Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare;
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups. Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse

16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and/or guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.
